data.title: OpenAI Accuses Apple of Pressuring Suppliers to Avoid Working With It
data.description:
ChatGPT developer OpenAI has filed counterclaims against iPhone maker Apple (AAPL). OpenAI alleges that Apple has pressured suppliers not to work with it and made it harder to hire former Apple employees. The November 27 filing adds to a legal battle that began in July, when Apple sued OpenAI over alleged trade secret theft. The dispute comes as OpenAI prepares to enter the consumer electronics market after its $6.4 billion deal to acquire a hardware startup founded by former Apple designer Jony Ive.

According to Bloomberg, OpenAI claims that Apple has asked manufacturers to reveal details about their projects with the AI company. Some suppliers reportedly fear that working with OpenAI could put their much larger Apple contracts at risk.

In one example, OpenAI alleges that a supplier moved its manufacturing work to the night shift to avoid conflicts with Apple's projects. That reportedly increased OpenAI's costs.

The problem is that OpenAI needs these manufacturers to build its upcoming devices. If suppliers are afraid of upsetting Apple, OpenAI could have fewer companies willing to produce its hardware. OpenAI also claims that Apple's employment agreements make it harder to recruit engineers. One provision prevents former Apple employees from recruiting their previous colleagues for a year.

Why Apple and OpenAI Are Fighting Over AI Hardware

The dispute comes as OpenAI prepares to compete more directly with Apple. With help from Ive, OpenAI is developing devices that would allow people to use ChatGPT without needing an iPhone. That could eventually threaten Apple's hardware business if consumers begin using AI devices for tasks they currently perform on smartphones.

However, Apple has its own accusations against OpenAI. Its July lawsuit alleges that former employees took confidential engineering information to help develop competing products. OpenAI denies those allegations and has asked the court to dismiss Apple's lawsuit. In October, it agreed not to use the trade secrets that Apple claims were stolen after a judge indicated that such an order was likely.

OpenAI has also accused Apple of benefiting from its confidential information. It alleges that a former employee who returned to Apple transferred more than 100 private files about unreleased OpenAI devices to personal accounts. Those files reportedly included product designs and manufacturing information.

Apple denies wrongdoing. It says that its policies prohibit employees from using confidential information belonging to previous employers and that it found no evidence supporting OpenAI's allegations.

The lawsuit is currently scheduled to go to trial on July 19, 2027.

data.title: Why Did Invesco QQQ Trust ETF Close Higher on Black Friday?
data.description:
Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100 index (NDX), closed 2.69% higher at $650.99 during Black Friday's shortened session. This came as tech stocks pulled major U.S. indices higher, closing the week on a high note. This followed volatile trading over the past few days, minus the Thanksgiving Thursday pause. For the Invesco QQQ ETF, memory chipmaker Micron (MU) stood out among its top holdings, rising 7.60% to $646.95.

Invesco QQQ ETF Rises as Chip Stocks Rally

Micron is the fund's sixth-largest holding, accounting for 3.32%. Of the ETF's $446.53 billion in total assets, $14.73 billion is in Micron.

Micron shares joined the rally in memory and storage stocks. This is despite a new warning from research firm TrendForce. In its new report, TrendForce said prices for conventional DRAM chips may continue to rise through 2027, but at a slower pace over time.

Apart from Micron, shares in chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) rose 4.56% to $424.54. AMD is the seventh-largest stock in the QQQ, accounting for 3.24%.

Of note, NAND flash memory maker SanDisk (SNDK) led the rally in memory and storage stocks, rising 15.96% to $85.36. SanDisk is also a key holding in the QQQ portfolio.

How Did Other Tech Stocks Perform?

  • Tesla shares (TSLA) climbed 5.22% to close at $400 amid the tech rally. The jump also came as a report noted that the EV giant is pushing to buy a German manufacturer of humanoid parts. Humanoid robots are part of Tesla's anchor growth plans.
  • Amazon shares (AMZN) rose 3.96% on Friday, closing at $254.12. This followed the rally in tech stocks. Interestingly, data from Adobe Analytics (ADBE) showed that Americans spent a record $7.1 billion shopping on Thanksgiving Day this year. This could benefit Amazon, as the company has expanded its Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals to 12 days. This is the longest such deal extension in the company's history.

Is QQQ a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

The Invesco QQQ Trust ETF has a Strong Buy rating. This reflects TipRanks' unique ETF analyst consensus. This method relies on a weighted average of analyst ratings on the fund's holdings.

In addition, the average QQQ price target of $880.01 suggests about 35% upside.

data.title: SpaceX's Wireless Expansion Could Make Anterix's Spectrum Worth Billions
data.description:
Satellite internet company SpaceX (SPCX) could become a potential buyer of wireless spectrum owned by Anterix (ATEX), a small U.S. telecommunications company whose stock has more than tripled this year. Anterix controls the country's largest collection of 900 MHz spectrum licenses, with roughly 85% still available. The company is valued at approximately $1.5 billion despite generating just $7.4 million in revenue over the past 12 months. However, no deal with SpaceX has been announced.

Wireless spectrum refers to the radio frequencies that allow phones to communicate. Anterix's frequencies are particularly valuable because they can travel long distances and pass through buildings more easily than higher-frequency signals. That makes them attractive to SpaceX, which wants to expand Starlink's satellite-to-phone service and potentially compete directly with mobile providers such as AT&T (T) and Verizon (VZ).

According to Bloomberg, Anterix has traditionally leased its spectrum to electricity companies. However, it is now considering larger sales to companies that could put those frequencies to different uses.

Interestingly, SpaceX has already spent billions acquiring wireless spectrum. In October, it purchased an additional 800 MHz of licenses from Grain Management in a deal reportedly worth $8 billion. SpaceX also asked regulators in August to make it easier to use the 900 MHz band for satellite communications, a proposal that Anterix publicly supported.

Anterix Could Also Benefit from Recent Changes in U.S. Regulations

Anterix could also benefit from recent changes in U.S. regulations. In February, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which regulates wireless frequencies, approved wider channels for the 900 MHz band. In simple terms, this allows companies to use more of those frequencies together, which could improve the amount of data they can transmit.

Then, in October, the FCC proposed allowing certain frequencies that were previously reserved for ground-based communications to also be used by satellites. This matters because Anterix's spectrum has traditionally been used by electricity companies to communicate with equipment on the ground. If regulators allow satellites to use those same frequencies, Anterix could potentially sell its remaining licenses to companies such as SpaceX.

The company has already completed a successful test that used its frequencies to communicate with a satellite. However, that does not mean its spectrum is ready for a commercial satellite-to-phone network.

Anterix still needs to make technical changes to its frequencies and move existing users out of certain channels before they can be used more efficiently. The company reported $107.5 million in cash and no debt at the end of September, which gives it money to help fund that work.

There is also regulatory uncertainty because the FCC has not yet approved all the proposed changes that would make the spectrum suitable for satellite communications.

data.title: Tether Buys $10 Million in Bitdeer Stock (BTDR) After 87% Drop to 52-Week Low
data.description:
Stablecoin issuer Tether bought $10 million of Bitdeer Technologies Group (BTDR) stock on Wednesday after the Bitcoin (BTC-USD) miner fell 87% from its 52-week high. That purchase lifted Tether's stake to 41.45 million shares, a Friday Schedule 13D/A filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission showed.

Bitdeer shares closed Friday's shortened session up 1.64% at $3.10 after closing Wednesday at $3.05. BTDR stock touched a 52-week low of $2.605 on Wednesday, far below its $20.72 peak. Tether bought 3.72 million Class A shares at a weighted average near $2.69. These new shares sat on a paper gain of about 15% at Friday's close.

Tether Repeats Bitdeer Dip-Buying Bet Despite Earlier Paper Losses

Wednesday's trade echoes Tether's February buy, when SEC filings showed the firm bought about 5 million Bitdeer shares near $8.41. Tether later sold 627,021 BTDR shares in June around $20.22, roughly 140% above its February entry.

That June sale left Tether holding about 98% of its Bitdeer position through the slump. Those 37.73 million Bitdeer shares were worth roughly $763 million in June and fell near $101 million at Wednesday's purchase price. Tether's stake in Bitdeer then grew nearly 10% after Wednesday's buy.

Even so, its ownership fell from 19.7% in June to 17.9% because Bitdeer's Class A share count expanded 21% to 231.8 million by Sept. 30, SEC filings showed.

Bitdeer Losses and Share Dilution Test AI Data Center Shift

Bitcoin mining still drives most sales at the Singapore-based company. Self-mining brought in $217.5 million of Bitdeer's record $320.7 million third-quarter revenue, while AI cloud sales added $20.4 million, its Nov. 10 SEC earnings release showed. Bitdeer held just 47 Bitcoin at quarter-end after selling almost all of the 3,855 coins it mined. This leaves sales directly exposed after Bitcoin dropped near $55,000 last week.

Large spending to convert mining sites into AI data centers widened Bitdeer's third-quarter net loss to $125.5 million from $30.1 million a year earlier, the SEC filing showed. Bitdeer has signed about $2.9 billion in AI cloud contracts and plans to launch its Tydal site in Norway first. "Customer prepayments, together with project-level financing, are designed to fund AI capacity as it is contracted. Our priorities are clear: deliver Tydal, complete our financings and bring Malaysia online," Chief Financial Officer Michael G. Potter said in the Nov. 10 filing.

Is Bitdeer a Good Stock to Buy?

Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on Bitdeer stock (BTDR) based on six Buys and one Hold. The average 12-month BTDR stock price target of $16.43 indicates 424.9% upside potential. (See PLTR stock forecast)

data.title: U.S. Dollar Nears Three-Month Winning Streak While Yen Approaches 160 and Pound Outpaces Euro
data.description:
The U.S. dollar neared a three-month winning streak on Friday while the Japanese yen approached 160 per dollar and the British pound outpaced the euro. British sterling held near $1.31 and the euro dropped below $1.094 as traders priced in December rate hikes from four central banks.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index has risen 1.8% in November for a third straight monthly gain and its longest run since 2024. This advance beat every Group-of-10 peer this month, while the ICE U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) edged up 0.09% to 103.76 on Friday. Fed funds futures price a 99% chance of a quarter-point Federal Reserve rate hike on Dec. 9. Markets also see a 64% chance of another Fed move in January after U.S. third-quarter growth hit a 4.3% annual pace on Wednesday.

Tokyo Inflation Pushes Bank of Japan Toward December Rate Hike

Japan's yen weakened against the dollar on Friday, pushing USD/JPY up 0.18% to 159.54, as higher U.S. Treasury yields drew buyers into the U.S. currency. The move came despite data showing Tokyo core inflation hit a 16-month high of 2.9% in November, Reuters reported.

Hotter consumer prices keep the Bank of Japan on track to lift its benchmark rate toward 1.50% next month, economists told Reuters.

Still, the dollar's climb toward 160 yen has revived talk of currency buying from Tokyo officials. "Better risk conditions could quickly bring back focus on intervention, especially if we get a hawkish hike from the FOMC on December 9," MUFG strategist Derek Halpenny told Reuters.

HSBC strategist Daragh Maher wrote that intervention risks should keep the pair near the top of a 156-to-160 range. He added that those warnings stop short of making 160 an official ceiling.

Euro Drops Below $1.094 After Pablo Hernandez de Cos Wins ECB Nomination

The euro (EUR/USD) fell 0.31% to $1.0936 against the U.S. currency on Friday. Currency markets barely moved after European Union leaders nominated former Bank of Spain Governor Pablo Hernandez de Cos on Thursday. He is set to succeed Christine Lagarde as European Central Bank president in February.

Eurozone inflation has climbed to 4% after tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz lifted energy costs. Officials held the ECB deposit rate at 2.50% in October after two earlier increases, and analysts expect a 25-basis-point hike to 2.75% on Dec. 17. Slower eurozone growth and weak German consumer confidence have still left the euro trailing the dollar and sterling.

Bank of England Rate Bets Hold Pound Near $1.31 and Lift Sterling Against Euro

Sterling (GBP/USD) edged down 0.09% to $1.3095 against the dollar on Friday while strengthening to 83.51 pence per euro. Traders expect steeper rate rises in Britain after the Bank of England lifted its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 4% on Nov. 5.

Money markets price an 80% chance of another Bank of England hike in December and a further increase in February, LSEG data showed. Britain's economy grew 0.7% between July and September, up from 0.5% in the prior quarter, while October retail sales rose 0.7%. Next Friday's U.S. nonfarm payrolls report will test whether the dollar can keep its lead into year-end.

data.title: Why Did Intuitive Machines Stock (LUNR) Jump on Black Friday?
data.description:
Shares of U.S. space tech infrastructure firm Intuitive Machines (LUNR) jumped by 9.41% to $10 in Black Friday's shortened trading session. This came amid a broader rally in tech stocks, which lifted the entire U.S. stock market. Interestingly, recent positive updates from the company may have also helped to fuel the rally in LUNR Stock.

Notably, Intuitive Machines rallied by 11.11% to $9.75 on Monday. LUNR and other space-related stocks climbed as the AI chip rally spread to the sector. This came after chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, briefly boosting overall stock market sentiment.

What Other Updates Could Be Behind the Rally?

On November 23, Intuitive Machines announced a key update. The firm said it has completed the preliminary design review for the Stirling Technology Space Research Experiment (START).

The project aims to convert heat from a radioisotope nuclear source into electricity. This helps provide continuous power and heat when sunlight is insufficient.

START is a project the company is developing in partnership with the U.S. Space Operations via Nuclear Enhanced Technology (SONET) team. SONET is part of the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory.

The project aims to solve a key power-and-heat problem lunar projects face. Spacecraft designed to run on solar power and batteries can run out of energy or become too cold to function during the long lunar night.

Meanwhile, Intuitive Machines also made another important announcement on November 9. The firm was now on a short list of companies NASA could hire to deliver equipment and run missions on the Moon. This is for the U.S. space agency's next-generation Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) 2 program.

data.title: Walmart Stock (WMT) Goes Flat as Coachella Music Festival Sues over Trademark Infringements
data.description:
Walmart (WMT) failed to get a tune out of its stock price today after it was revealed that the companies behind the Coachella music festival in California were suing it for trademark infringement. Coachella Music Festival and GoldenVoice, which produce the festival, are claiming that the retail giant has repeatedly sold merchandise bearing Coachella's trademarks without a license. This is despite demands from the two companies dating back as far as 2017 for it to stop doing so. The WMT share price is up 18% in the year-to-date.

Complaints Have Not Worked

The complaint, first reported by Music Business Worldwide, was filed earlier this week in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California.

"Despite having no association with Plaintiffs or Coachella, Walmart has intentionally sold, and allowed others to sell, directly competitive goods bearing the Coachella Marks and has used, and allowed others to use, without authorization, the Coachella Marks in advertising for these goods via Walmart's stores, both physical and online," the complaint alleges.

It adds that it has made repeated requests and demands for Walmart to cease selling and advertising infringing goods both online and in its stores, and to remove or alter its advertising, signage, products, and promotional materials.

"Plaintiffs' requests have been of minimal benefit; Walmart typically stops for a period of time, but then resumes its infringing conduct," it said.

Walmart is also accused of using photographs taken on the festival grounds, showing Coachella's Ferris wheel, in what the complaint describes as advertising for its Dr. Thunder soft drink.

Restraining Order on Walmart

In April 2023, the complaint alleges, Walmart's store in La Quinta, California, used signage "copied directly from Plaintiffs' line-up posters from prior festivals" to promote items including beverage coolers and folding chairs.

The plaintiffs are seeking a temporary restraining order, as well as preliminary and permanent injunctions barring Walmart from selling or advertising goods in connection with the Coachella marks. They are also seeking financial damages.

Aside from the potential financial hit, Walmart may also suffer a blow to its corporate reputation. Coachella is a popular event with around 125,000 attendees and stars such as Sabrina Carpenter playing on stage.

It is why legal and regulatory issues are part of the risks associated with investing in Walmart. That is according to the TipRanks Risk Analysis tool for WMT.

data.title: SK Hynix Doubles Daily Share Buyback Orders After Stock Decline
data.description:
South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix (SKHY) has doubled its daily share buyback orders to about 700,000 shares, up from 350,000, as it tries to support its falling stock price. The move comes as the company pursues a massive 100 trillion won, or $75 billion, shareholder return plan for 2026. Despite record profits from AI demand, its U.S.-listed shares have fallen by roughly 21% from their $149 July offering price.

According to The Korea Herald, SK Hynix increased its planned daily purchases because management believes that the recent selloff has left its shares undervalued.

Share buybacks allow companies to purchase their own stock using available cash. When those shares are canceled, the total number of shares decreases. This means that existing investors own a larger percentage of the business without purchasing additional stock.

SK Hynix has already completed a 40 trillion won buyback program, with those shares canceled on November 5. The company also approved another 20 trillion won in repurchases in October. Half of that amount is intended for share cancellations, while the other half will be used for employee compensation.

What's Next for SK Hynix's AI Memory Business?

One reason that SK Hynix can afford these massive buybacks is the growing demand for its high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips. These chips help AI processors handle large amounts of information quickly, which makes them important for AI systems.

The company expects its newest HBM4 chips to account for more than half of its HBM shipments and revenue in the fourth quarter. It also plans to bring its M15X production facility to full capacity by the end of 2026.

Meanwhile, SK Hynix has signed long-term supply agreements with 14 major customers, including large cloud computing companies. These contracts generally last five years and already cover more than 50% of its total production capacity for 2027 and 2028.

However, there are risks. Research firm TrendForce recently warned that conventional memory chip prices could start falling in 2028 if demand for servers slows down and supply increases. That could put pressure on SK Hynix's profits, even if its AI memory business continues growing. The company also expects to spend significantly more on manufacturing equipment and production facilities in 2027 as it prepares to meet future demand.

data.title: How Does the S&P 500 Typically Perform in December?
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SPX) is just a few days away from December, which has historically been one of its strongest months of the year. Seasonality data suggest the benchmark index has a good chance of finishing the month higher, although performance during midterm election years has been somewhat weaker.

According to Carson Investment Research, December has been the S&P 500's most consistent month, producing positive returns 73.3% of the time since 1950. The index has also averaged a gain of 1.4% during the month. December has only been the worst-performing month of the year once over that period.

However, December isn't always a standout month in terms of returns. It has been the strongest month of the year only four times since 1950, compared with 12 times each for April and November.

How Does December Perform During Midterm Years?

The seasonal picture is a little different during midterm election years. According to Time-Price Research, the S&P 500 has averaged a December gain of 0.90% during midterm years, finishing higher in 15 of 24 instances, or 62.5% of the time. That compares with an average December gain of 1.27% across all years in its longer-term dataset.

Other historical data also point to a modest December gain during midterm years. The Market Calendar puts the average at 0.34%, compared with 1.26% across all years.

For investors, the takeaway is that December has historically favored the bulls. However, the pattern is less reliable during midterm years. The S&P 500 has a history of finishing December higher, although that doesn't guarantee another positive month in 2026. Investors will still need to keep a close eye on interest rates, economic data, and earnings as the year comes to a close.
